title: client-signal-sprintbacklog-compact-notes-2024-09-17
content:
Purpose:
Compact working notebook that folds recent field signals into a short sprint-backlog and cost-aware sketch of implementation options. Not an exec brief — this is for product/engineering pairing and quick cadences with Solutions/CS.

Approach / notes-to-self:
- Source window: calls + support logs + onboard interviews (Aug 1 - Sep 10, 2024). Quick sample: 12 enterprise touchpoints (finance, search SaaS, knowledge base, compliance tooling).
- Method: rapid affinity -> cost bucket -> feasibility band (quick / medium / heavy).
- Bias: we bias toward low-risk fixes that reduce ops volume and obvious latency friction. Keep a handful of mid-term bets for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Unresolved: which of these need full SLOs vs. quick UI toggles? mark below.

Highlighted customer quotes (verbatim, trimmed):
- "We love the model speed but the token cost spikes make predictions unpredictable when our batch size jumps." — trial user, analytics startup
- "Prefix caching is good but sometimes the cache misses blow up cost — can we expose cache hit ratio per customer?" — platform team at national bank
- "Embedding recalls are noisy; need a rerank shim or built-in semantic filters." — product lead, docs search vendor

Raw themes (3 clusters):
1) Observability + actionable metrics
   - ask: per-customer cache hit-rate, per-route cost-variance, sampled token-level traces
   - pain: customers can't correlate spikes to prompts or batch sizes; support tickets escalate to eng.
   - quick idea: add a "cost spike" alert template + exposure in Console logs (toggle).

2) Cost-control UX primitives
   - ask: simple knobs to cap tokens/cost per request, safe-fallback models, burst policies for Dedicated
   - pain: engineering teams resort to client-side hacks (shortening prompts) or maintain fallback logic in app code.
   - quick idea: per-route throttle + model-fallback config in Console (can be stored as route policy).

3) Quality-to-cost tradeoffs for embeddings and reranking
   - ask: recommended quantization / model family mapping for high-throughput retrieval workloads; built-in simple reranker option (cheap model)
   - pain: customers experimenting with quantization settings that break quality without guardrails.

Backlog (prioritized, compact) — columns: title | why | estimated effort | cost impact | tentative owner
- "Expose cache hit metrics per-customer" | reduces tickets, helps tuning | quick (1 sprint) | medium (saves tokens) | owner: Aisha
- "Route policy: safe-fallback to cheaper variant" | preserves availability, cuts unit cost during overload | medium (2–3 sprints + infra) | high | owner: Eng-serving-runtime
- "Per-route token cap + request sampling UI" | stops runaway bills; faster triage | quick | medium-high | owner: Product-hosted-api
- "Embeddings: recommended profiles + small reranker" | improves retrieval quality at low cost | medium | medium | owner: Applied-ML
- "Cost-spike alert playbook + canned Slack/Email" | reduces MTTR for customers | quick | low | owner: Customer-success ops
- "KV-cache debug tool (trace replay)" | deep-debug for SREs + SEs | heavy (infra + privacy review) | high savings long-term | owner: SRE + infra

Quick wins (ship in <= 2 sprints)
- Add a Console toggle: "Show cost per-request sample" (sampled traces, anonymized). Low infra, high immediate clarity.
- Draft a support KB article + default alert template for "token-cost spike".
- Implement per-route token cap in Console UI (frontend only) that enforces client-side pre-checks (server enforcement TBD).

Medium-term (3–6 sprints)
- Route policy + fallback implementation with A/B canary. Must coordinate with Release/Platform to avoid regressions.
- Embedding profiles + a simple reranker pipeline (cheap cross-encoder or logistic model). Requires benching and eval sets from Solutions.

Heavy / exploratory
- KV-cache replay/trace infrastructure — needs privacy review and storage controls. Tied to Dedicated customers first.
- Fine-grained SLA metrics and per-token billing invariants (legal/finance coordination).

Cost & tradeoffs (sketchy estimates)
- Console toggles & KB: ~$10–15k (mostly eng + docs). ROI: reduces 20–30% of low-effort support tickets.
- Route policy / fallback: infra + runtime dev ~ 8–12 sprints across teams. Can cut peak token spend by up to 40% for affected routes.
- Embedding reranker: model dev + infra ~ 4–6 sprints. Token cost per query increases slightly but net improves hit precision -> fewer downstream calls.
- KV-cache replay: high infra cost (storage + privacy flows) but can save lots on debugging time and big customers' OPEX.

Risk notes / constraints:
- Any telemetry that surfaces customer prompt content -> legal/privacy red flags. Default: only surface hashed prefixes and token counts; full-text only with explicit consent and redaction.
- Fallback models must be behaviorally compatible (sampling/temperature controls) to avoid UX regressions.
- Changes that affect per-token billing require finance sign-off and customer comms calendar.

Open questions (to answer before scoping)
- Which customers get early access? propose: top 10 Dedicated + 5 Hosted customers who reported issues.
- Do we expose cache hit-rates in the Console by default or opt-in? recommend opt-in (privacy).
- How to measure embedding reranker efficacy? need an eval harness + aligned metrics (precision@k, latency tail).

Immediate next steps (for next weekly sync):
- [Maya] Draft a one-pager (2x slides) for PM sync summarizing the 3 quick wins + ask for 2 sprints of eng time for toggles.
- [Aisha] Prototype Console UI mock for token-cap and cost-sample toggle. Link: https://figma.com/redwood/mock-token-cap (wip).
- [Tomás] Run a basic cost simulation for route-fallbacks on 3 customer workloads (CS-4821, CS-4850, CS-4899) and drop numbers into spreadsheet.
- [Ben] Start a small eval dataset for embedding reranker: collect 50 queries + human labels (redact customer PII).

Notes, logs, references (quick links):
- Slack: #cs-field-voices thread 2024-09-04 (summary pinned)
- Linear: CS-4821 (token spike analysis), CS-4850 (cache visibility request)
- GH PR: repo: console PR #218 (cost-sample telemetry change)

Short-term communication plan:
- Share a short note + prototype in the CS weekly. Ask 10 customers for quick opt-in (benefit: early visibility, lower support load).
- No public docs until we validate metrics and privacy approach.

Appendix (scratch):
- Quick heuristic: if cache_hit_rate < 0.6 and per-request tokens > 1500 -> auto-suggest token cap of 1200 and recommend embeddings rewrite.
- TODO: make a small linear ticket to track Privacy review for trace capture (owner: Legal eng contact: Priya S.).

End of compact notebook. Keep this lightweight and iterate — will convert to a formal playbook if customers opt-in and numbers look good.
